> Куратор: froze-контекст проводного протокола агента — регистрация executor'а, клеймы назначений, отчёты, discovery v3, native intake; текст апстрима (EN), статус v0.1-draft.

# vesmaro-agent ↔ vesmaro-eyes board — wire protocol

- **Status: v0.1-draft** — the freeze target for the Go agent rewrite.
  The board side (mnemos-eyes 1.22+) implements §1–§2 today; §3 (discovery
  leg) lands server-side separately and is specified HERE first so both
  sides converge on one text. Anything not written here is not a contract.
- **Source of truth (behaviour):** the Python reference implementation,
  `mnemos-eyes/scripts/assignment_poller.py`, and the board routes in
  `mnemos-eyes/server/app.py` (ADR 0009 + Amendment 2).
- **Precedence:** on conflict, ADR 0009 (lifecycle, A1–A4) and Amendment 2
  (multi-executor, two clocks) win over this document; this document wins
  over any implementation.

## 0. Conventions

| Topic | Contract |
|---|---|
| Transport | HTTPS, TLS with the lab CA **pinned** (fail-closed: no CA, no connection; never `InsecureSkipVerify`) |
| Direction | **Outbound-only.** The agent opens NO listening ports; the board has no inbound channel to the machine (ADR 0009 §9). Ingress/network policy of the host stays unchanged. |
| Tokens | Two classes: enrollment `mne_…` (single-use, TTL 15 min) and the executor secret (long-lived bearer). Tokens travel ONLY in the `Authorization: Bearer` header — **never in a query string, never in a URL, never in logs** (board contract ADR 0012 §9). |
| Secret exposure | `executor_secret` appears in EXACTLY one response body ever (§1). The agent keeps it in memory or a 0600 env file; never in the YAML config, never in agent prompts. |
| Logging hygiene | Transit credentials are never persisted. Log hygiene order is **mask first, truncate second**: a credential-shaped substring is replaced with its prefix (`mne_…`, 8 chars) BEFORE any length cap applies, so truncation can never re-expose a tail. |
| Clocks | Two-clock discipline (Amd 2 §6): assignment clocks (claimed > 10 min without start, running > 30 min without heartbeat → expired) belong to the board reaper; presence clocks (online ≤ 120 s, stale ≤ 600 s) belong to the registry. The agent never writes presence directly — presence ticks ride authenticated calls only. |
| Caching | All board answers carry `Cache-Control: no-store` (ADR 0012 §9). The agent must not persist board responses beyond the process lifetime. |
| Payload caps | The agent enforces caps BEFORE sending (pre-truncate): a 422 on complete/fail would retry forever and end as `unreported`. Caps: report `body`/final report ≤ **16384**; fail `reason` / heartbeat `note` ≤ **2000** (server trims further); `claimed_by` ≤ **120**; `claim_token` ≤ **64**; fail stderr tail ≤ **400** chars (`STDERR_TAIL_CHARS`, server caps the stored note at 2000); envelope over stdin ≤ **60000** bytes (`STDIN_ENVELOPE_CAP`, §2.8). |
| Presence thresholds | online ≤ 120 s, stale ≤ 600 s — SERVER-OWNED constants delivered in the registry `meta` (`GET /api/executors` → `meta.presence.{online_max_age_s,stale_max_age_s}`); the agent reads them from meta, never hardcodes. |
| Time | ISO-8601 UTC everywhere. |

### Error-code conventions

Client errors are the board's FastAPI contract: `401` bad/missing
credential · `403` identity mismatch or revoked · `404` unknown id ·
`409` conflict/illegal transition · `410` spent enrollment token ·
`422` validation (unknown harness, malformed payload) · `429` rate/cap ·
`503` board side-effect disabled (fail-closed). Transport failures are
NOT protocol errors — §2.7 defines the retry budgets.

## 1. Registration lifecycle

### 1.1 Enroll — `POST /api/executors`

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer mne_…` (the one-time enrollment token the
owner minted in the board UI; mintable ≤ 3 live, rate 3/10 min).

```json
// request
{"name": "vps-1", "harness": "zcode", "host": "vps-1",
 "transport": "local-poll", "version": "0.1.0"}
```

- `name` — 1..120 chars, unique across the registry; the UI/owner picks
  it (the bootstrap convention: hostname).
- `harness` — MUST be a value of the board's harness dictionary
  (`GET /api/harnesses`, wave 3C); unknown values are rejected — the
  agent validates against the dictionary BEFORE sending (honest local
  error beats a round-trip 422).
- `version` — **the VERSION handshake** (§5): the agent's own version,
  stored on the registry row and visible to the owner at approve time.
  Optional, default `""`, ≤ 60 chars; the board's own version is readable
  from `GET /api/health` (`app_version`) — the agent MAY log the pair at
  startup as the skew fact.
- **WHO enrolls (ratified):** in M1 the AGENT performs the enrollment
  itself — the binary runs an enroll mode (`vesmaro-agent --enroll
  --url <board> --token mne_… [--name …] [--harness …]`) that registers,
  persists `executor_secret` to the 0600 env file and prints the
  bootstrap verdict. The bootstrap installer only DELIVERS the token and
  the binary; this makes the VERSION handshake real (the secret's
  registration row carries the agent's actual version, not an
  installer-echoed constant). The interactive UI enrollment path stays
  for humans.

Responses:

| Code | Body | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | `{"ok": true, "executor": {...}, "executor_secret": "…"}` | registered, `state: pending`; **`executor_secret` is shown EXACTLY ONCE** — hash-only server-side (claim_token pattern, long-lived). The agent stores it (memory/0600 env) before the process may exit. |
| 401 | — | token unknown |
| 409 | — | duplicate `name` — surface to the user with the `--name` hint; NEVER auto-retry with a suffixed name (the owner must see the collision) |
| 410 | — | token expired/used/revoked — surface "mint a new token"; never re-send the same token |
| 422 | — | unknown harness / bad transport / validation |
| 429 | — | rate (10/60 s) or pending-cap |
| 503 | — | server-side auth not configured (fail-closed) |

The single-use CAS (token `created→used`) rides the SAME server
transaction as the registry INSERT: a rolled-back registration never
burns the token, and two competing registrations of one token produce
exactly one winner (the loser sees 410).

### 1.2 Pending → approved → working leg

The agent lands in `state: pending`, `enabled: false`, capabilities `[]`
(owner-declared only, never self-expanded). **Approve and enable are two
separate owner actions on the board, entirely OUTSIDE the agent** — the
agent polls its own state (via §4) and surfaces
"awaiting approval / approved but disabled / ready" honestly. The agent
MUST NOT treat approval as its own concern; it just keeps the presence
clock ticking (pending executors MAY tick presence; revoked may not).

Revocation (`state: revoked`) is terminal: the secret stops opening the
machine loop immediately (kill-switch). The agent must stop the working
loop on a persistent 403 from any machine-class call and say so.

## 2. The working loop

Preconditions: the executor row is `approved` AND `enabled`. The board's
routing never nominates anything to a pending/disabled/revoked executor.

### 2.1 Poll + presence piggyback — `GET /api/assignments?state=queued&executor_id={id}`

Open read (no bearer required to READ), interval 10 s ± 2 s jitter.
**Presence piggyback:** when the request carries `executor_id=` AND the
agent authenticates with ITS OWN executor token, the board ticks that
executor's `last_seen` (auth-gated: an open read must not let arbitrary
readers fake liveness — presence feeds the auto-pick routing tier).
This tick is the only liveness the idle agent emits.

Response: `{"ok": true, "count": N, "items": […]}`; every item carries
`id, task_id, specialist, harness, executor_id, state, spec_hash,
routing{resolved, reason}` — and NEVER `claim_token` or `spec_snapshot`
(those exist only in the claim answer, §2.2). `spec_hash` travels in the
item: the refusal report and the audit journal cite it.

**`executor_id` is NOT a filter** — the server returns ALL queued
assignments regardless. The agent skips LOCALLY, before any claim:
an item whose `executor_id` is set and differs from the agent's own id
is another executor's pin — skipped silently (no claim attempt: the
board's spoofing gate would answer 403 and pollute the audit on every
tick). Items without a pin are claim candidates for any agent.

### 2.2 Claim — `POST /api/assignments/{id}/claim`

Auth: executor token. CAS on `state='queued'` — two claimers, one 200,
one 409; correctness is structural.

```json
// request
{"claimed_by": "vps-1", "executor_id": "ex-…"}
```

| Code | Body | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | `{"assignment": {…}, "claim_token": "…", "task": {…}}` | the answer carries `spec_snapshot` + `spec_hash` — **the agent executes ONLY the snapshot, never the live spec** (A2, anti-TOCTOU). `claim_token` is a correctness boundary (a stale claimant cannot finish a re-claimed assignment) — not a secret. |
| 409 | — | lost the race / an explicit pin names ANOTHER executor |
| 403 | — | the assignment is explicitly pinned to this executor but a DIFFERENT token presented it (spoofing gate) |

An explicit `executor_id` pin is enforced server-side: the pinned
executor's token claims it, nothing else. The agent MUST send its own id
honestly and never claim another executor's pin (CWE-290 gate).

### 2.3 Start — `POST /api/assignments/{id}/start`

Auth: machine class + `{"claim_token": "…"}`. `claimed → running`.
Claim without start > 10 min → board reaper expires the assignment.

### 2.4 Heartbeat — `POST /api/assignments/{id}/heartbeat`

Every 60 s while the child process is alive; body
`{"claim_token": "…", "note": ""}`. **A 409 answer is a KILL SIGNAL**
(reaper/cancel raced the heartbeat): the agent terminates the child
(SIGTERM → 10 s grace → SIGKILL, asynchronously — heartbeats of other
children never block). Transport failure on heartbeat is retried on the
next beat; the child is NOT killed for it.

Heartbeats also tick the assignment clock; a running child without a
heartbeat for 30 min is expired server-side.

### 2.5 Complete / Fail

- exit 0 → `POST …/complete` `{"claim_token": "…", "final_report": "…"}`;
  if the harness produced no final report, the agent writes the fallback
  `exit 0, agent report above` — the launcher contract owns a final
  report existing, not its content.
- exit ≠ 0 → `POST …/fail` `{"claim_token": "…", "reason": "process
  exit N: <stderr tail ≤ 400>"}`.
- Both answer `{"ok": true, "assignment": {…}, "task": {…}, "moved": [...]}` —
  additive response fields are listed in §7.

**The REPORTS channel (the agent's own voice — the child writes here):**
`POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/reports`, machine-class bearer (the same
`VESMARO_BOARD_TOKEN` env the child inherits):

```json
// request
{"kind": "intermediate" | "final", "body": "<report ≤ 16384>",
 "agent": "<executor_name ≤ 120>"}
// 201 — "superseded" is a LIST of report ids it replaced (decode as
// []int, never an int — an int decode fails on every 201)
{"ok": true, "report": {…}, "superseded": [101, 102]}
```

Errors: `404` unknown task · `422` validation (kind/body/agent) ·
`429` rate **30 reports / 60 s** (the envelope's REPORTS block tells the
child to batch). Reads are OPEN: `GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/reports` →
`{"ok": true, "task_id": "…", "count": N, "items": [{id, kind, body,
agent, …}]}`.

**Final-report detection (fallback decision):** at child spawn the agent
snapshots `_final_report_ids` — the ids of `kind: "final"` items (a
record without an int `id` is skipped with a warning: malformed input
may only push toward the fallback, never crash the loop). Before
`complete`, the set is re-read; a NEW final id means the agent wrote its
own final and `final_report` stays empty; otherwise the fallback text is
sent. No clock math — pure id diff.

### 2.6 Recovery sweep (start-time)

On every agent start: own `claimed|running` assignments are failed
unconditionally (tokens are lost with the old process; nobody can finish
them) — this closes the at-most-once window.

Wire details: the sweep reads TWO lists
(`GET /api/assignments?state=claimed` and `?state=running`), selects OWN
rows by `claimed_by == executor_name` (the config identity the previous
process claimed with), and fails each **WITHOUT a claim_token** — the
fail route accepts the executor token by IDENTITY: the token-backed
executor id must equal the assignment's `claimed_by_executor`. (The
`claimed_by`-string fallback is board-token class ONLY — the laptop
poller's legacy trust; the Go agent is executor-token class and never
sends `claimed_by`.) A local pid remembered in the audit journal gets a
best-effort SIGTERM if its argv still matches.

### 2.7 Board unavailability

The agent NEVER dies from board errors. Per-operation budgets: poll →
skip the tick, log, retry next tick; claim/start → log, leave the
assignment untouched; heartbeat → retry next beat (child stays alive);
complete/fail → 5 attempts, then journal `unreported`. Only start
conditions are fatal: no token, unparsable config, lock already held —
distinct exit codes.

### 2.8 Envelope execution (the allowlist)

The assignment is delivered to the harness as the canonical envelope
(launch prompt): `[GCW ASSIGNMENT {id} | task {task_id}]` header,
`MODE: assignment-run` marker, goal, verbatim acceptance criteria,
REPORTS block. Delivery is DATA — stdin, or written to a temp file when
the allowlist template names `{envelope_file}`. No shell interpolation
of spec content, ever.

The launch gate is the LOCAL allowlist: exact `(harness, specialist) →
argv` templates from the local config. Miss → **fail-closed**: skip the
assignment (it stays `queued` server-side) + ONE machine-written refusal
report to the task (citing `spec_hash`). The board nominates; the agent
decides (A3). Templates may use `{specialist}` and `{envelope_file}`
placeholders; spec content is never interpolated into argv (the argv is
built with a strict formatter — the snapshot never passes through a
shell). `specialists: ["*"]` trusts a whole harness explicitly.
`max_concurrent` children cap: at capacity the tick is skipped (nothing
lost, nothing refused).

**Envelope delivery and caps:** stdin by default; if the template names
`{envelope_file}`, the envelope is written to a 0600 temp file in the
state dir and its path substituted. An envelope over
`STDIN_ENVELOPE_CAP = 60000` bytes CANNOT go via stdin (the write would
block): the launch is refused as failed (`launch refused: envelope N
bytes exceeds stdin cap — use {envelope_file} delivery`) and the
assignment is failed with that reason — the honest fix is switching the
template to `{envelope_file}`.

**Order is fixed: claim → SPAWN → start.** The child exists before
`start` is sent; if `start` fails (transport beyond budgets, 409), the
child is terminated (SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL) and the assignment is
failed with the same `claim_token` — otherwise the task would lie
in-progress with a live unclaimed child and the reaper window would be
undefined.

**Child environment:** exactly `CHILD_ENV_KEYS = (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR,
LANG, VESMARO_BOARD_TOKEN)` present in the parent env — a minimal,
unprivileged profile. The secret is the ONLY credential the child ever
sees (it needs it for its own REPORTS posts, §2.5).

**MANAGED-block auto-lock (optional hardening, off by default):** the
allowlist SECTION between the MANAGED marker lines refuses external
modification while the agent runs; entries below the marker stay
user-owned. Section-level, not per-entry — one marker, one rule. The
marker format is defined HERE (protocol authority): the section opens
with the exact line `# --- MANAGED: managed by vesmaro-agent; edit
freely below this line ---` and extends to end-of-file — everything
inside is agent-managed (the bootstrap installer ADOPTS this format in
its next wave; today's installer-written blocks follow the same
managed-header/user-tail shape informally).

**AGW-17 addendum — the bounded region and the enabled tri-state:** the
agent's own rewrite (0.3.0) bounds the region with a closing marker,
the exact line `# --- /MANAGED ---`: everything ABOVE the open marker
and BELOW the close marker is user-owned and preserved byte-identical
on every regeneration. The managed entries live under the dedicated
top-level key `managed_allowlist:` (never merged into the user's
`allowlist:` — no YAML duplicate-key hazard by construction) and
replay through the SAME AllowlistEntry shape with one new field:
`enabled` is tri-state — absent/`true` = active, explicit `false` =
an INERT discovery stub (never dispatchable; the effective allowlist
is user-allowlist + enabled managed entries). Region invariants:
idempotent rewrite (identical content = no write), atomic
(temp+rename), YAML-validated before rename, mode-preserving, cap 32
entries with LOUD overflow. Gate flag: `discovery_managed_allowlist:
auto|off` (default `auto`); `off` leaves the file untouched entirely.

**AGW-18 addendum — the mesh-mode child channel (the loopback board
shim):** under `transport: mesh` the child's REPORTS wire (§2.5) is
re-terminated ON the agent; the executor secret NEVER leaves the agent
process. The live pilot (§5.3) proved children post natively (ADR 0009
§7) but cannot reach the board from behind the relay, so:

- The agent runs a loopback-only HTTP shim (bind `127.0.0.1`, kernel
  port, logged at start; started BEFORE the first spawn, stopped with
  the agent). Surface — a MINI-BOARD: exactly
  `POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/reports`, with the board's answer relayed
  VERBATIM (201 created; 404 unknown task; 422 validation; 429 rate —
  never softened). A down relay leg answers an honest `503` JSON (the
  child retries per ITS policy; the shim never hangs, never invents a
  verdict). Everything else is a clean `404` JSON (the reserve for
  future board paths — they simply do not exist here yet).
- Child environment in mesh mode (amends CHILD_ENV_KEYS for this
  transport ONLY): `VESMARO_BOARD_TOKEN` is WITHHELD and
  `VESMARO_BOARD_URL` (the shim's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) is added.
  The direct transport keeps the frozen profile byte-for-byte. The
  shim takes NO credential from the child — the loopback boundary IS
  the check; the agent attaches the executor secret on the mesh leg
  itself (G3). A child that still sends a token-shaped header is
  ignored, not rejected.
- Envelope (Appendix A) in mesh mode: `board_url` renders the SHIM URL
  and the REPORTS auth line names the local shim instead of the token;
  direct-transport envelopes stay byte-identical to the frozen
  template.

### 2.9 Native intake (AGW-19, ADR 0021)

Under `transport: mesh` the SAME loopback listener carries a second
route — the **native Canon intake** — while the compat route of the
§2.8 addendum stays a dumb pipe byte-for-byte (the board remains its
sole validator; deprecation is out of scope).

- **Route:** `POST /intake/v1/{capability}/reports`, where
  `{capability}` is an unpredictable per-child token (16 crypto/rand
  bytes, hex-encoded) minted from the spawn registry at claim time and
  handed to the child in `VESMARO_BOARD_URL`
  (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/intake/v1/<token>`; the envelope's
  `board_url` renders it too). An unknown caller is a **404 BEFORE the
  body is read** — the loopback boundary alone trusts any local
  process (CWE-346); the capability closes anonymous writes. The
  compat route deliberately carries NO capability: existing children
  know the bare shim URL (§5.3 pilot); capability on compat is a
  separate, future decision.
- **Composite route (review-2):**
  `POST /intake/v1/{capability}/api/tasks/{task_id}/reports` — the
  path a REAL child's posts land on when the envelope's REPORTS line
  renders `<board_url>/api/tasks/{id}/reports` over the capability
  URL (ADR 0009 §7 children, e.g. the Pi CLI through the envelope).
  It is served as a COMPAT relay (`PostReportVerbatim`, board
  statuses verbatim — the child posts the ADR 0009
  `{kind, body, agent}` form, which the strict Canon edge would
  reject by construction) but under the SAME capability gate BEFORE
  the body is read: the token is resolved against the spawn registry,
  and an unfamiliar caller is a `404` before any `io.ReadAll`. The
  `{task_id}` URL segment is IGNORED — attribution is registry-based,
  exactly as on the native route; the segment is only the child's
  own spelling of the board path. This closes the deferred review-1
  decision (capability on compat semantics) for the one compat route
  a registry-backed child can reach. The route exists only when the
  intake is mounted.
- **Restart boundary (AGW-22):** a restart of the agent is the
  declared loss boundary for IN-FLIGHT lane records — accepted
  (`202`) but undelivered reports die with the process and leave NO
  dead-letter row (the letter fires on delivery outcomes and drops,
  neither of which a `kill -9` produces). The accept answer already
  told the child the report was queued; the child's own retry policy
  is the recovery path, and a `202` is not an ACK — it is an honest
  "the agent's lane took it", bounded by the agent's uptime. This is
  deliberately NOT a durability contract in v0.5: there is no
  on-disk queue, and pretending one would be the silent degradation
  this protocol refuses everywhere else. The v0.6 candidate is an
  on-shutdown drain — close the lanes with a timeout, letter the
  undelivered with a `transport-agent-shutdown` class — a
  graceful-stop improvement, never a crash guarantee. Compat
  children never had a lane: their `503`-on-relay-down + retry path
  is unchanged by restarts, as it always was.
- **Attribution:** the intake resolves `task_id → child` from the
  spawn registry WITHOUT child participation, plus a grace window
  (default 15 min) after the child's death for late reports. A task
  outside the registry+window is a `404` — matching board semantics.
- **Body cap:** the native edge enforces the same 1 MiB cap
  (`MaxShimBodyBytes`); an over-cap body is an honest local `413`
  (reason class `oversize-body`), never a transport masquerade.
- **Canon record (mandatory format of the native channel):** the body
  is a Canon record `{title, tags, metadata.canon, body}` validated by
  the go:embed-pinned `report.schema.json` (draft 2020-12,
  `santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6`; the envelope `$ref` resolves from
  the embedded bytes — network fetch at validation time is forbidden).
  The pin carries a sha256 checksum contract; a pin≠canon-HEAD
  divergence fails the workspace pin test (the CI route; Actions are
  billing-blocked).
- **Normalization BEFORE validation** (the agent absorbs what the
  child cannot know, never pushes it into the harness): the §8 tag
  triple (`project:<slug>` from the executor context, `agent:<slug>`
  from the attribution, `mnemos:session` — the §3-mapped report
  subtype), `period` (derived from arrival time, ISO week
  `2026-W40`), `language` (config, default `ru`), and the title
  (derived from the first body line, rune-capped at 80). Fields the
  child supplied correctly are NEVER rewritten. The three proven
  checks port from canon's validate.py: schema-pass +
  `x-canon-sections` (each required H2 present as an exact
  `^## <name>$` line) + title (non-empty, single line, ≤ 80).
- **Strict is the default.** A soft mode exists only as a rollout
  window with an explicit expiry: `intake_soft_mode: until:<RFC3339>`
  — a soft window without a date is REFUSED at startup (the flag
  carries its own death). Inside the window a failing record is a
  `202` with `accepted: false` plus the named defect, and the record
  dead-letters; after the window the answer is a strict `400`. The
  ladder is normalize → warn → reject.
- **Status matrix (the edge's own verdicts, all JSON):** `202`
  accepted at the edge (the delivery is asynchronous — the lane, not
  the board, was filled); `400` + machine-readable reason on
  rejected(validation); `404` unknown capability/task; `405` non-POST;
  `413` over-cap; `429` when the per-task lane buffer is full (the
  record is dropped VISIBLY — a counter, a journald log line (the
  intake's audit surface is the agent's own log; no JSONL-audit claim
  here), a dead-letter row — and the child's own retry policy
  applies). The 202-vs-201
  split is deliberate: 201 on the compat route means the BOARD stored
  the row; 202 on the native route means the agent took it into its
  lane.
- **Lanes and pool:** per-task serial FIFO (lane capacity 1–2, one
  worker per task) plus a global semaphore (~8) shared by all lanes on
  the relay calls — one noisy task cannot eat the mesh leg (CWE-770).
  Delivery rides `PostReportVerbatim` verbatim: the relayed write is
  the board's OWN `POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/reports` form
  (`ReportCreate`: `{"kind": "intermediate"|"final", "body": <the
  canon record's body TEXT — the markdown the owner reads>, "agent":
  <the attributed child slug>}`; extra fields would be silently
  ignored board-side, so none travel). The `kind` follows canon §7:
  `final` when the record's `metadata.canon.status` is `resolved`
  (reserved for reports), `intermediate` otherwise. A record body over
  the board's 16384-CHARACTER cap is a `413` PRE-accept with the
  `oversize-board` reason class (runes, not bytes — the board counts
  Python `len()` on str): never an accepted record dying post-accept
  on a 422. The board stays the gate for its own fields.
- **Outcome taxonomy (canon archcom-v1, ADR-0003 SLI corrections):**
  accepted / normalized+accepted / rejected(validation) /
  dead-letter(transport). `rejected(validation)` is EXCLUDED from the
  dead-letter denominator; the dead-letter rate divides transport
  deaths by delivered volume (NO-DATA until the first delivery). A
  board refusal AFTER acceptance is a transport death, not a
  re-litigated verdict; its reason classes:
  `transport-relay` (mesh leg down), `transport-board-4xx`,
  `transport-board-rate` (the board's 30/60 s budget),
  `transport-board-other`.
- **Dead-letter:** a working queue, never a graveyard — JSONL under
  `<state-dir>/dead-letter/` (0700 dir, 0600 files), secrets masked
  BEFORE the write (Bearer tokens, `VESMARO_*` values, long hex/base64
  runs, key-like assignments; children are arbitrary LLM code — the
  payload is untrusted bytes), each row carrying
  `{ts, task_id, reason_class, reason, payload_sha256, payload_masked}`,
  TTL 7 days + 10 MiB per file with rotation (default 5 files), replay
  manual only. Dead-letter > 10%/day signals a broken contract.
- **Metrics (emitted since v0.5, gating the v0.6 move):** the intake
  emits a JSON metrics snapshot line every 5 minutes and on SIGUSR1:
  `reports_submitted`, `accepted`, `normalized_accepted`,
  `rejected_validation` (per reason class), `dead_letter` (per reason
  class), `dropped_by_backpressure`, `reports_per_task`,
  `time_to_visible` p50/p95 (accept → board confirmation, sliding
  window), and the dead-letter rate per the taxonomy above. There is
  NO scrape endpoint (S3 keeps the surface loopback-only); the log IS
  the observability plane.

## 3. Discovery leg — `POST /api/executors/{id}/discovery`

v0.1-draft: specified HERE first; the board route lands in a following
mnemos-eyes wave. Purpose: feed the board's harness dictionary/UX with
what is ACTUALLY installed on the machine — the owner sees "zcode is
here, aider is not" without SSH.

```json
// request (auth: THIS executor's token; content-type json)
{"harnesses": [
  {"name": "zcode", "version": "1.22.0", "path": "/usr/bin/zcode"},
  {"name": "claude-code", "version": "", "path": "/usr/local/bin/claude"}
]}
```

- `name` — harness-dictionary spelling where known; local ad-hoc names
  allowed (the board DROPS entries whose `name` is not in its dictionary
  — unknown values never auto-extend the dictionary; dictionary growth
  is a ui-token owner act, wave 3C).
- `path`/`version` — best-effort, may be empty strings.
- Discovery is ADVISORY: it never creates registry rows, never extends
  allowlists, never changes routing. It is a mirror of local fact.
  Drops of unknown names are AUDITED BOARD-SIDE (the server's audit
  trail records what it dropped and from whom) — the agent's duty is
  only to send facts, honestly and best-effort.

**AGW-17 addendum — environment facts:** the request carries an
additive top-level field next to `harnesses`:

```json
{"harnesses": [{"name": "zcode", "path": "/usr/bin/zcode"}],
 "environments": [
   {"name": "copilot", "kind": "cli", "home_path": "/home/u/.copilot",
    "markers": ["agents", "skills", "state"], "version": "0.9.x",
    "config_paths": ["/home/u/.copilot/agents"], "session_hints":
    {"store": "projects", "count": 42}}]}
```

- `kind` — `cli` | `service` | `ide-extension`. The facts are built from
  a built-in fingerprint table over the configured `discovery_roots`
  (home dot-dirs, `.aider*` glob rows, `.vscode*/extensions` rows);
  every reported path exists on disk at scan time.
- CONTENT-FREE by construction: the scan performs stat/glob existence
  checks only — it never reads foreign config content. `session_hints`
  carries a table-verified store NAME and a file COUNT; session/project
  names and contents never leave the machine.
- `version` — best-effort `--version` of the harness binary when it
  resolves on PATH (cli rows only); omitted otherwise.
- Board-side acceptance is UNCHANGED: unknown fields are additive and
  the route contract above governs the `harnesses` list. STATUS
  (verified 2026-09-26 against the live board's OpenAPI, 1.37.1): the
  discovery route is NOT deployed board-side yet — the agent's posts
  answer 404 and stay silent below info (the contract above defines
  what the future board wave must accept; a board that ignores the
  additive `environments` field stays correct).
- The agent's OWN allowlist wiring from these facts is the MANAGED
  auto-allowlist (§2.8 AGW-17 addendum): disabled-by-default records
  for discovered CLI environments, gated by
  `discovery_managed_allowlist: auto|off`, with the one-shot
  `--discovery-once` leg (scan + regenerate + report, no board
  contact) for operators and bootstrap flows.

**Capabilities inventory addendum — discovery v3 (2026-09-28):** each
`environments[]` row MAY carry an additive `capabilities` object — the
NAMES-ONLY inventory of what the harness hosts:

```json
{"name": "zcode", "kind": "cli", "home_path": "/home/u/.zcode",
 "capabilities": {
   "specialists": ["bathys-researcher", "gcw-tech-lead"],
   "specialists_count": 39, "gcw_specialists_count": 38,
   "skills": ["a11y-audit", "ab-testing-design"],
   "skills_count": 121,
   "plugins": [],
   "instructions": ["architectural-committee.md"],
   "instructions_count": 24,
   "notes": {"agents_md": true, "gcw_managed": true}}}
```

- Fields: `specialists` (+`specialists_count`, +`gcw_specialists_count`
  for the gcw-* prefixed share), `skills` (+`skills_count`), `plugins`
  (+`plugins_count`), `instructions` (+`instructions_count`), `notes`
  (booleans). Every list is sorted; every counter is the FULL total —
  the lists are capped (`specialists`/`skills` ≤ 50 names,
  `plugins`/`instructions` ≤ 30) and the whole object is further capped
  at **8 KiB of marshaled JSON per environment** (over budget the lists
  shrink again; the counters never do). Empty lists and empty
  inventories are OMITTED (`omitempty`) — a v2 payload without the
  field stays byte-identical.
- **Names, never contents** (secret discipline): agent/skill/plugin/
  instruction NAMES are public facts; file CONTENTS never leave the
  machine. Exactly two bounded content-read exceptions exist, each
  emitting booleans or a name list only: (1) pi `agent/settings.json`
  is parsed for the `packages[]` names alone (string `"npm:x"` and
  object `{source:"npm:x"}` forms; nothing else from the document is
  emitted); (2) zcode `AGENTS.md` is probed for the single `gcw:begin`
  marker line (the GCW-install marker → boolean
  `notes.gcw_managed`).
- Per-harness layouts (best-effort; an absent directory is an empty
  list, NEVER an error): **zcode** — `agents/*.md` stems (specialists),
  `skills/*/SKILL.md` dir names, `gcw/instructions/*.md` filenames,
  `plugins/` direct children, notes `agents_md`/`gcw_managed`;
  **pi** — `agent/settings.json` packages[] names plus
  `agent/extensions/*` filenames (both in the `plugins` slot), note
  `agents_md`; **copilot** — `agents/*.md` stems (the GCW
  `x.agent.md` spelling reduces to `x`), `skills/*/SKILL.md` dir
  names, `instructions/*.md` filenames, `installed-plugins/` direct
  children (`state/` is session data, not inventory); every OTHER
  harness kind gets a generic probe of `agents/`, `skills/`,
  `extensions/` under its home. IDE-extension rows and file homes
  (glob rows) carry no inventory (the field is omitted).
- Known pi limitation: pi has no environment fingerprint row in the
  v2 table yet (table growth is an owner act — a row would also
  surface pi in the MANAGED allowlist zone), so the pi scanner answers
  from the day that row lands.
- Board-side acceptance is UNCHANGED (additive unknown-field rule, §3
  AGW-17 addendum); the `harnesses` list and the v2 environment fields
  are untouched.

### 3.1 Presence heartbeat — `POST /api/executors/{executor_id}/heartbeat`

The idle agent's liveness tick (when it has no queued claim to piggyback
on, §2.1). Executor-token class; **identity-match**: the URL `id` MUST
equal the token's executor identity — a mismatch is `403` and NEVER a
404 (an unknown id never confirms what exists); `revoked` executors are
`403` (kill-switch: presence must decay); `pending` executors MAY tick
(the owner sees liveness before approving). Body:
`{"note": "≤ 2000"}` (usually empty; the server IGNORES the body — it
exists for wire symmetry). Rate budget: **60 / 60 s** — the
10-second poll piggyback (§2.1) makes an explicit heartbeat rare.
Response: `{"ok": true, "executor": {…}}`. No SSE — clients render ages
from the registry read.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | ticked — `last_seen` refreshed |
| 401 | executor token required |
| 403 | identity mismatch / revoked |
| 429 | rate (60/60 s) |

Cadence: only when the poll loop is otherwise idle longer than the
presence budget (§0, thresholds from registry `meta`). Failure to
heartbeat is retried next beat; it is never fatal and never logged above
info.

## 4. Health / status

There is NO agent health endpoint and NO listening socket: health is a
board-side fact (executor registry presence) plus local process facts
(journald/audit log). `GET /api/health` (board, open) answers board
liveness and carries `app_version` (§5); the agent's own verdict for
operators is the audit journal + `systemctl status`. Presence decay to
`offline` is the board's honest "agent probably not running" signal.

### 4.1 State read — `GET /api/executors/{executor_id}`

OPEN read (same boundary as the registry list). Answers the FULL registry
row — the verdict machine of §1.2 and `ExecutorState()` are implemented
ON this contract:

The answer is FLAT — the row itself, no `ok`/`executor` wrapper
(response_model `ExecutorOut`; the WRAPPED `{ok, executor}` shape is the
§3.1 heartbeat answer — decode accordingly or the Go decoder silently
yields a zero-struct):

```json
{
  "id": "ex-…", "name": "vps-1", "harness": "zcode", "host": "vps-1",
  "transport": "local-poll", "capabilities": [], "version": "0.1.0",
  "enabled": false, "state": "pending", "last_seen": "…",
  "presence": "online", "registered_via": "", "registered_at": "…",
  "updated_at": "…"
}
```

`404` unknown id. The verdict mapping (§1.2): `pending` → "awaiting
approval"; `approved` + `enabled: false` → "approved but disabled";
`approved` + enabled + `presence: online` → ready; anything else →
"registered but not seen / revoked". No `secret_hash`/`executor_secret`
ever travels (hash-only storage; the plaintext existed once, §1.1).

## 5. VERSION handshake

- The agent sends its own version in `POST /api/executors` (`version`
  field, §1.1) and MAY send per-harness versions in discovery (§3).
- The board surfaces the agent version on the registry row
  (`executors.version`) — the owner sees "this machine runs agent 0.1.0"
  at approve time and in the settings card.
- The agent reports `--version` locally (build-time injection, single
  source: the `VERSION` file at repo root).
- The handshake fires because the AGENT enrolls (the `--enroll` mode,
  §1.1 — ratified): the registration row's `version` is the binary's own
  fact, not an installer constant.
- Version skew agent↔board is tolerable per §2.7 (unknown JSON fields
  are additive-only and ignored; REMOVING a field is a protocol major
  bump).

## 6. Security requirements (from the wave-4 security review — 7 P2, all binding)

| # | Requirement | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | **Transit credentials never persist.** The enrollment token and the executor secret live in memory and (optionally) a 0600 env file. Never in the YAML config, never in command lines (`ps` visible), never in the audit journal, never in error strings. |
| S2 | **Mask → truncate, in that order.** Any log line that may carry a credential-shaped string is masked (prefix + `…`) BEFORE truncation; truncation must never re-expose a masked tail. Applies to audit JSONL, journald lines, and error wrapping. |
| S3 | **Outbound-only invariant.** No listening sockets, no inbound handlers, no NAT hole. The agent's network posture is exactly: HTTPS requests it initiates. A regression here is a release blocker. |
| S4 | **Allowlist fail-closed.** Missing/parses-empty/unparsable allowlist = refuse everything (with refusal reports), never "run everything". The launch decision contains no LLM and no heuristic — exact `(harness, specialist)` match only. |
| S5 | **MANAGED auto-lock (optional).** The allowlist SECTION between the MANAGED marker lines (format defined in §2.8; the bootstrap installer adopts it in its next wave) refuses external modification while the agent runs; user-owned entries below the marker stay user-editable. Section-level, not per-entry — one marker, one rule. Off by default in v0. |
| S6 | **Snapshot discipline (A2).** The agent executes the claim-time `spec_snapshot` only; the live task spec is never fetched, never rendered into the envelope. |
| S7 | **Token-class discipline.** The enrollment token opens ONLY registration (§1.1). The executor secret opens machine-class calls. The agent never sends the enrollment token after §1.1 completes, and never sends the executor secret to any URL other than the configured board (TLS-pinned, no redirects across hosts — redirect following is disabled). |

## 7. Compatibility

The Go agent is a drop-in replacement for the Python poller against the
same board version: same routes, same auth classes, same envelopes, same
env-variable contract (`VESMARO_BOARD_TOKEN` — historical name, do not
rename). Config is YAML with the same keys; `discovery_extra: [paths]`
is a Go-side ADDITION (feeds §3, ignored by the Python poller).

### 7.1 Config keys and defaults

| Key | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `board_url` | required | base URL, pinned-TLS |
| `executor_id` | `""` | set at registration; empty = never-ticking presence |
| `executor_name` | required | the claim/sweep identity |
| `poll_interval` | `10` | seconds |
| `poll_jitter` | `2` | **`0` is LEGAL** — deterministic polls (python parity); the agent must not silently coerce it |
| `heartbeat_interval` | `60` | seconds |
| `max_concurrent` | `2` | children cap |
| `ca_bundle` | system trust | missing file = fail-closed refusal to start |
| `allowlist` | — | §2.8; absent/empty refuses everything |
| `managed_allowlist` | `[]` | AGW-17 addition (§2.8): the agent-owned region between the MANAGED markers; merged into the effective allowlist (disabled stubs stay inert) |
| `discovery_managed_allowlist` | `auto` | AGW-17 addition (§2.8): `auto` regenerates the MANAGED region at start; `off` leaves the config file untouched |
| `discovery_roots` | `[$HOME, /var/home/abyss]` | AGW-17 addition (§3): the home directories the environment scan walks; each root is best-effort (an absent path is skipped) |
| `audit_path`, `lock_path` | `~/.local/state/vesmaro-agent/…` | DELIBERATELY distinct from the Python poller's paths — the two agents never share state |
| `discovery_extra` | `[]` | Go addition (§3) |
| `transport` | `direct` | Go addition (AGW-15): `mesh` = the board API relayed verbatim through mnemos-mesh `AssignmentRelay.CallBoard` |
| `mesh_endpoint` | required when `transport: mesh` | the mesh **relay's agent-leg** bind — the `relay.agent_listen` of a mnemos-mesh node running `role:relay`. NOT the node-role gateway leg (`gateway.listen`, default 8791): that leg serves only the memory-class AgentGateway, and in a `role:relay` process the gateway section is config-REJECTED (role purity). Their CI relayfixture binds `127.0.0.1:0` (kernel-assigned; the relay logs `agent_listen` on stdout) — a production operator takes the address from the relay's config/log |
| `mesh_ca_bundle` | required when `transport: mesh` | the mesh CA root PEM — the mesh leg has no plaintext mode |
| `mesh_token_file` / `mesh_token_env` | one required when `transport: mesh` | the **mnemos-minted agent token** (G3: rides gRPC `authorization` — attribution; 0600 file). A LIVE pilot token waits for their AgentGateway Phase B invite flow (not landed at mesh-core v0.3.0); their relayfixture uses a fixture-token class for tests. Do not invent issuance |
| `mesh_pin` | `""` | optional relay-leaf fingerprint pin (`sha256:<hex>`), the mesh-core agentclient form |
| `intake_soft_mode` | `off` | Go addition (AGW-19, §2.9): the native intake's rollout window — `off` (STRICT, the ratified default) or `until:<RFC3339>`; a soft window WITHOUT a date is REFUSED at startup, a past date likewise (the flag carries its own death) |
| `intake_language` | `ru` | Go addition (AGW-19, §2.9): the fallback record language the intake normalizes into records the child left incomplete (the owner's language, configurable) |
| `dead_letter_path` | `<state-dir>/dead-letter` | Go addition (AGW-19, §2.9): overrides the dead-letter JSONL directory (0700 dir / 0600 files); REQUIRED under `ProtectSystem=strict` unit hardening whenever the state dir lives outside the unit's `ReadWritePaths` — a read-only death store is a startup failure |

### 7.2 Agent exit codes

Deliberately DIFFERENT from the Python poller (which returns 2 for both
a bad config and a missing token, 3 for the lock): the Go agent splits
them so monitoring can tell the causes apart.

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| 0 | clean run / verdict delivered |
| 2 | bad arguments or unparsable config |
| 3 | no `VESMARO_BOARD_TOKEN` in the environment |
| 4 | singleton lock already held |
| 5 | registration refused (4xx, §1.1 scope only) |
| 6 | enroll-mode post-registration failure: env/yaml write or systemd enable failed (§1.1 scope; the working loop has no systemd business) |

### 7.3 Additive response facts (ignore-unknown applies)

`complete`/`fail` answers carry `{ok, assignment, task, moved}`; the
registry list carries `meta.presence` thresholds and the sweeper
interval; assignment items carry `routing{resolved, reason}`, `topics`,
`spec_hash`. Unknown JSON fields are additive-only and MUST be ignored
(§5); REMOVING any named field is a protocol major bump.

### 7.4 Update / rotate

Re-registration and secret rotation are the bootstrap installer's
contract (`deploy/poller/bootstrap.sh` in mnemos-eyes): spent-token
re-run = UPDATE (artifacts refreshed, user allowlist preserved); rotation
= revoke + delete on the board, then a fresh `--enroll` with a new token
and the same name. The agent implements the enroll MODE (§1.1) and never
re-registers silently behind the operator's back.

The parity checklist lives in the repository README.

## Appendix A — the assignment envelope (frozen template)

Rendered STRICTLY from the claim response (`spec_snapshot`, A2) — the
live task spec is never read. The bearer token is deliberately not a
template parameter: it cannot leak into the prompt by construction (the
child finds it in its inherited environment, §2.8). Field fallbacks:
`GOAL` ← GOAL section or first sentence of the snapshot; `ACCEPTANCE` ←
AC section or the explicit "treat the snapshot checklist" notice;
`DEPENDS` ← `—`; `memory_id` ← literal `-` when the assignment carries
none. The snapshot is fenced (```` ``` ```` or longer, chosen
so the fence never appears inside the snapshot).

**Mesh-mode amendment (AGW-18, §2.8 addendum):** under `transport: mesh`
the `board_url` is the agent's loopback report shim and the REPORTS
auth line is the shim variant (no child-side token exists). Direct-
transport envelopes remain byte-identical to this frozen template.

```text
[GCW ASSIGNMENT {aid} | task {task_id} | mnemos {memory_id}]
MODE: assignment-run
SPECIALIST: {specialist} (harness: {harness}, executor: {executor_name})

This is an assignment-launch: the MODE marker above is the only
legitimate sign of one. Work strictly from the SPEC SNAPSHOT at the
bottom — it is the immutable execution view taken at assignment
creation; do NOT re-read or re-fetch the live task spec.

GOAL: {goal}

ACCEPTANCE (verbatim from the snapshot):
{acceptance}

DEPENDS: {depends}

SCOPE: task {task_id} only, as specified in the snapshot. Anything
outside this scope is out of bounds — open a mnemos open-question
instead of doing it.

REPORTS (primary channel, ADR 0009 §7):
- intermediate report at every meaningful milestone;
- a final report is ALWAYS required before you exit 0;
- POST {board_url}/api/tasks/{task_id}/reports
  body: {"kind": "intermediate"|"final", "body": "<report>", "agent": "{executor_name}"};
- auth: Bearer token from the env var VESMARO_BOARD_TOKEN already set
  in your environment — never print, quote or log its value;
- budget: at most 30 reports per 60 s — batch your updates.

RIGHTS (WF-1 §4.2): work only on your own assigned tasks. Finishing
your work moves the task to resolved; acceptance (resolved → done) is
the owner's / Tech Lead's call — self-acceptance is forbidden.

ESCALATE: on a blocker you cannot resolve, exit non-zero with a short
reason as the last line of stderr — the poller reports it as the
assignment failure. Never hang waiting for input.

SPEC SNAPSHOT (verbatim; sha256 {spec_hash}):
{fence}
{snapshot}
{fence}
```

Delivery: stdin by default; `{envelope_file}` templates get the envelope
as a 0600 temp file (path substituted before spawn). Over 60000 bytes
via stdin → launch refused (§2.8).
